title: Pool a fixed set of database connections
description: ConnectionPool manages a fixed number of reusable Connection objects. acquire() hands out an available connection, or throws if none are free. release() returns a connection to the pool. The pool is pre-filled at construction — connections are never created on demand. Fill in acquire() and release().
hints: Use a Queue or List to track available connections
acquire() should remove and return one connection from the available set
release() should add the connection back — but only if it belongs to this pool
issues: Creating a new database connection for every request is expensive and slow
Without a pool there is no upper bound on concurrent connections
overallGoal: Use the Object Pool pattern to maintain a fixed set of Connection objects that are borrowed and returned rather than created and destroyed.
goals: Pre-populate a Queue<Connection> in the constructor with the requested number of connections
In acquire(), poll the queue and throw IllegalStateException if it is empty
In release(), add the connection back to the queue
